# Alzheimer's disease

Rising to the global challenge of Alzheimer’s disease through innovation and collaboration.

[A woman in a white blouse sits at a cafe table, smiling, holding a coffee cup, with a laptop open.
The atmosphere is cozy and relaxed.]

## Challenge

Alzheimer’s disease is a chronic medical condition that leads to increasingly severe memory
impairment and behaviour and social challenges. It’s not a part of normal ageing and is one of the
biggest public health challenges of our time.1

Over 55 million people are living with dementia - and with prevalence projected to increase to
nearly 140 million by 2050, the impact of Alzheimer’s will intensify as populations age.1 The
disease eventually takes away a person’s ability to live independently, requiring family and friends
to provide increasing levels of care, while medical costs also increase.

Many of us at Roche have been personally touched by Alzheimer’s disease. We understand the heavy
toll it takes on all those affected - our grandparents, our parents, our partners and our children.
This human connection, our passion for patient-centric science and solutions and our mission to
reduce the impact of Alzheimer’s on society fuel our persistence in this complex disease area for
our and your loved ones.

## Focus

We believe acting early in Alzheimer’s disease is going to have the greatest impact on society. It
will help people living with Alzheimer’s today receive better care and tomorrow’s people living with
Alzheimer’s receive effective treatments, to help retain their independence for longer.

#### Following the science

Together with our many partners, we are working towards the day when the term “Alzheimer’s disease”
no longer invokes feelings of stigma, despair, loneliness and isolation – a day when we detect it
early, slow it down, or even stop its progression and help preserve what makes people who they are.

With over two decades of scientific research in Alzheimer’s, we have made meaningful contributions
to the field by driving understanding of the biology and underlying pathology of the disease and
have persisted when faced with disappointments. We continue to listen to and closely collaborate
with the Alzheimer’s community, learning from setbacks and building on each success.

#### Transforming care together

We’re using our diagnostic and pharmaceutical capabilities in an effort to better detect, diagnose
and treat Alzheimer’s when symptoms first start to show and are actively working toward preventing
the disease altogether.

We understand that the challenges that exist in Alzheimer’s go beyond the capabilities of science.
Global challenges can only be overcome through global partnerships and we have entered into numerous
partnerships and collaborations that have provided valuable contributions to the field.

To advance scientific research, improve our understanding of the disease and the needs of those
touched by it, reduce stigmas and advance health impact, we will continue to collaborate with
equally passionate partners across academia, advocacy, government and industry – both within and
outside of healthcare.

**References**

1. World Health Organisation. Dementia. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/dementia

## Videos

#### Transcript

[00:00:05]

Alzheimer's disease is a medical condition caused by changes in the brain. It can affect memory,
behaviour, problem-solving skills and daily activities, with symptoms slowly getting worse over
time, affecting a person's ability to live independently. Scientists are still working to understand
exactly what causes Alzheimer's, but we know that the greatest risk factor is age. Genetics,
lifestyle and environmental factors may also contribute to someone's likelihood of developing
Alzheimer's.

[00:00:41]

Whilst Alzheimer's disease is not a normal part of ageing, it is more common in elderly people.
Another factor is genetics. In most cases, a family history of Alzheimer's disease increases your
risk, but doesn't mean you will develop Alzheimer's disease. The gene that is most strongly
associated with Alzheimer's is called apolipoprotein E, or APOE for short. APOE comes in different
forms—known as alleles. We inherit one allele from each parent. One of these alleles, APOE ε4, may
increase a person's risk for Alzheimer's disease by 8 to 12 times if they inherit two copies.

[00:01:22]

Genetic testing can identify which APOE alleles a person has. Lifestyle and environmental factors
may also contribute to someone's likelihood of developing Alzheimer's disease. Risk factors linked
to Alzheimer's disease include: hearing loss, lower education level, smoking, poor diet, lack of
exercise, depression and social isolation. Research suggests that 40% of dementia cases are
preventable by actively taking steps to lead a healthier lifestyle.

[00:02:03]

A healthy diet, good sleep, and regular exercise may help to protect against Alzheimer's disease.
Mental stimulation and social activity have also been linked to better brain health. For more
information about Alzheimer's disease and how it changes the brain, watch the next video in the
Science in Seconds series.

#### Science in Seconds

This six chapter series aims to demystify the science behind Alzheimer’s Disease. Throughout the
series we will touch on topics such as causes of AD, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment and research.

# Our SHE policies, guidelines and position papers

##### Policies

Our Corporate Principles serve as a guide for developing a broad range of measures and documents
related to safety, security, health and the environment (SHE) at Roche. Since the late 1970s all SHE
matters have been guided by a single corporate function: Group Safety, Security, Health and
Environmental Protection. Its activities are governed by a corporate policy that establishes
fundamental and binding principles and objectives.

##### Guidelines

Fuller, more specific guidance for the practice-oriented implementation of the SHE policy is
provided by the Roche Guidelines for the Assurance of Safety, Security, Health and Environmental
Protection. We supplement these with Guidance Notes for specific functions and topic-specific
Corporate Directives.

The Roche Guidelines are based on ISO Standard 14000 (Environmental Management Systems) and on our
many years of experience proactively managing SHE activities. The guidelines also cover commitments
that Roche has made as a signatory to the International Chamber of Commerce Business Charter for
Sustainable Development and as a member of the World Business Council for Sustainable Development
and the chemical industry’s Responsible Care® initiative.

Our SHE guidelines apply throughout the Group and take precedence over local legal requirements,
where they exceed those requirements. They also form the basis for local SHE manuals prepared by
Roche affiliates for local implementation.

##### Position Papers

Our policies and guidelines cover SHE issues in a general way. We periodically issue corresponding
Position Papers to address particular SHE issues.

# Itovebi (inavolisib) ▼

Itovebi (inavolisib) is an oral, targeted medicine used for the treatment of adults with hormone
receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative breast cancer whose
tumours are identified to have a *PIK3CA*-mutation - one of the most commonly mutated genes in
HR-positive disease. Itovebi works by inhibiting the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) protein,
which drives cell growth, proliferation and survival, and plays a pivotal role in disease
progression in HR+ breast cancer. Designed with a unique mechanism, Itovebi also works by
facilitating the degradation of the mutated PI3K alpha isoform while sparing other isoforms to help
minimise the overall burden and toxicity of treatment.

The Itovebi, in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant, is approved as a first line treatment
for adults with HR-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative, advanced
breast cancer with a PIK3CA-mutation in more than 60 countries, including the United States and
European Union.

# Our environmental goals and impact

#### Our goals

According to the principles of a sustainable development Roche is striving for a continuous
improvement also in the area of safety, security, health and environmental protection. This can be
achieved by changing behaviour, by adapting equipment to the most recent standards or developing new
innovative processes. However, a sustainable effect can only be obtained within a longer time frame.

Roche wants to further promote this trend of continuous improvement in the various areas of SHE and
achieve progress where ever it is possible and economically viable. In a series of workshops, aimed
at the Roche Group, as well as discussions with internal and external experts, mid-term targets have
been set for the period 2025–2029.

ambition (2029) for a 50% reduction of our total environmental impact (eco-efficiency for operations
and product stewardship score for products) and a goal to achieve real zero greenhouse gas emissions
from scope 1 & 2 (own operations and purchased energies) by 2050. For detailed background
information on the goals, please see:

# Infectious diseases

The infectious disease landscape is ever-changing with outbreaks, mutations, emerging pathogens, and
growing resistances placing pressures on healthcare systems. Roche is determined to provide relief
and care.

[image of two gloved hands holding a laboratory sample]

## Challenge

Infectious diseases caused by viral and bacterial pathogens represent an ever-growing medical need
for millions of patients worldwide. Combining a rich legacy in infectious diseases with the latest
science and technology platforms, Roche focuses on the discovery and development of novel treatments
to address some of the world’s most pressing health challenges.

## Focus

Infectious diseases are becoming increasingly difficult to manage. While much healthcare effort is
devoted to preventing the spread of disease and associated treatments, less attention is paid to the
impact these infections have on the broader healthcare landscape.

Currently, Roche infectious diseases research and development is dedicated to finding effective
treatment for a number of life-threatening infections that include influenza and multi-drug
resistant bacteria. These diseases, for which there is often a high unmet medical need, affect
millions of people worldwide in wide degrees of severity. For this reason, and to ensure each
patient receives the most appropriate and effective care, Roche has adopted different strategies to
tackle the spread of these infectious diseases – from focusing efforts against multi-drug resistant
bacteria into developing treatments for the the top three Gram-negative bacteria identified by the
World Health Organization as number one Priority Pathogens, to continuing to innovate treatment
solutions to prevent as well as treat influenza, or combining therapies that pair direct-acting
antivirals with immune-enhancing molecules to treat viral hepatitis.

Viral hepatitis is a major public health threat and a leading cause of death worldwide.¹ An
estimated 354 million people are living with hepatitis B or C, leading to around 1.1 million deaths
per year.

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health security challenge. Drug-resistant bacterial
infections cause deaths worldwide. The lack of effective antibiotics is threatening modern medicine,
making essential preventive and life-saving interventions increasingly difficult and allowing
hospital-acquired infections to spread.

# Breast Cancer

[A confident woman with natural curly hair wearing a pink turtleneck, looking thoughtfully at the
camera with a blurred green leafy background outdoors]

Breast cancer is a hugely complex disease. Our research and solutions aim to further our
understanding of breast cancer and improve outcomes for everyone affected by this disease.

## Challenge

There exists many types and subtypes of breast cancer, meaning every patient is different and thus
requires an individualised treatment approach.

Despite remarkable progress in this setting to date, some patients will see their disease return in
the long-term, which is why there is a critical need to continue to optimise early breast cancer
care and to do more to prevent the disease evolving to an advanced, incurable stage. By combining
pharmaceutical science, strong diagnostic, digital and genomic capabilities, we are able to innovate
and develop treatment options tailored to each individual’s needs. Our advanced diagnostic
solutions, and most notably the use of biomarker testing, bring us closer to fulfilling our
long-term ambition of offering patients personalised treatment approaches. It’s been an immense
challenge, but ongoing research efforts are finally bearing fruit for this challenging disease.

## Focus

We believe there is room for improving outcomes for people with breast cancer. Our focus lies in
identifying new targets, refining and exploring immunotherapy approaches, and investigating new
treatment combinations.

The advances in AI technology have revolutionized diagnostics, providing healthcare professionals
with more precise answers and allowing them to provide their patients with a wider array of
treatment options. Existing and new treatment options offer hope for those living with breast
cancer.

# Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD)

[Decorative image]

Through medical innovation and partnerships, we are providing new options to people living with
neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) to help them retain as much independence as possible.

## Challenge

NMOSD is a rare, lifelong and debilitating autoimmune disease of the central nervous system,
primarily damaging the optic nerve(s) and spinal cord. It affects around 200,000 people worldwide
and is most common among women, affecting people in the prime of their lives, usually in their 30s
and 40s.

People with NMOSD experience unpredictable, severe relapses directly causing cumulative,
irreversible, neurological damage and disability. One relapse may lead to permanent blindness,
muscle weakness, paralysis and, in some cases, death. Before targeted diagnostic and treatment of
NMOSD, within five years 50% of individuals with NMOSD required a wheelchair and 62% of people with
NMOSD were functionally blind.

The right help and support can bring stability to people with NMOSD and ease the burden of the
disease. This includes enabling people with NMOSD to take control of how their condition is managed
and treated, based on their changing needs, to help them maintain a sense of independence.

## Focus

At Roche we believe greater awareness of NMOSD will benefit all those living with the condition; we
are committed to the community through our ongoing research.

Only recently have we seen a significant advancement of our understanding of NMOSD, developing
in-depth knowledge and new treatments. At Roche, we are committed to playing a significant part in
this advancement, taking an innovative approach to research and development. By working closely with
partners and patients, we can continue to transform the lives of those living with NMOSD. We never
stop following the science, ensuring we’re doing now what patients need next, to help preserve what
makes people who they are.

#### Transcript

[00:01]

Neuromyelitis Optica, or NMO, is a rare disease that affects up to 5 people in every 100,000. NMO
often affects people in the prime of their lives.

NMO can take away someone’s sight, mobility, and independence in an instant — and leave them feeling
exhausted. It can profoundly impact the person, their family, and every aspect of their life.

The threat of another relapse is a constant worry. Day-to-day living can become unpredictable, and
the future uncertain.

The right help and support can bring stability to those affected by NMO

[01:43]

and ease the burden of the disease. This enables people to look to the future and plan ahead.

People with NMO want to do as much as possible, for as long as possible — and plan for a future
beyond NMO.

Shareholders may participate in the elections and votes exclusively by issuing authorisations and
instructions to the independent proxy, either in the form of written instructions sent by post or by
remote electronic voting (link below).

The written instructions form as well as the required login data for the remote electronic voting is
enclosed with the voting materials sent to the shareholders.

Shareholders may provide their written or electronic instructions (incl. the amendment of already
provided electronic instructions) by **Sunday, 13 March 2022, at 8.00 pm at the latest**. If a
shareholder issues instructions both by post and electronically, the instructions issued last will

# Frequently asked questions

Welcome to the Roche frequently asked questions. Here you will find guidance on careers, products,
clinical trials, grants, partnerships and more. If your question is not answered here, our contact
channels are available to help you.

### Careers and employment

#### How can I work for Roche?

We welcome talented people who are inspired by our purpose and values. You can explore our current
opportunities on the [Careers page][102] , where you will find openings across a wide range of
functions, locations and experience levels.

#### I have applied for a role. When will I hear back?

Our recruitment teams review every application carefully. If your experience matches the
requirements of the role, a member of the team will contact you about next steps. As we receive many
applications, response times may vary.

#### I cannot find a suitable role at the moment. Can I stay connected with Roche?

Yes. You can join our [Talent Community][103] or set up a candidate profile on the [Careers
site][104] . This allows us to keep you informed when roles that match your skills and interests
become available.

### Grants, scholarships, donations and sponsorship

#### How can I request a grant, scholarship, donation or sponsorship?

Requests of this nature are reviewed according to [Roche’s global philanthropy criteria][105] .
Please visit our [Philanthropy Criteria and Requests page][106] to understand our principles,
eligibility requirements, and submission process.

#### What kinds of initiatives does Roche support?

We support projects that create sustainable, meaningful impact in areas such as education, community
health and social development. We do not support projects linked to political, religious or
commercial interests, and we cannot consider informal or unsigned requests.

### Products and medical information

#### Where can I find information about Roche products such as Accu-Chek®?

Information on Accu-Chek® and other Roche products is available on their dedicated websites. These
platforms offer guidance on product use, support services, and contact details.
* For Accu-Chek®, [find more information here.][107]
* For Roche Pharma products, [find more information here.][108]
* For Roche diagnostics products, [find more information here.][109]

#### I have questions about orders or invoices. Whom should I contact?

For questions relating to orders, invoicing or product supply, please contact the relevant local
Roche organisation. Contact details are available on [ our website’s Locations section.][110]

### Partnerships and business enquiries

#### I am interested in partnering with Roche as a distributor or business partner. How can I
#### proceed?

If you are seeking a partnership with our Pharmaceuticals or Diagnostics businesses, please [contact
us here.][111] Your enquiry will be directed to the appropriate Roche team for review.

If you are a supplier or wish to explore supplier opportunities with Roche, please visit
[suppliers.roche.com][112] for guidance on registration, requirements and our supplier standards.

### Clinical trials

#### Why does Roche conduct clinical trials?

[Clinical trials][113] are an integral part of the drug and diagnostic discovery and development
process. Before a new medicine or diagnostic test can be made available, evidence of its safety and
effectiveness must be provided by well-designed, well-controlled, and carefully monitored clinical
studies in patients who consent to participate.

#### How can I register for a clinical trial?

Up-to-date information on ongoing clinical trials, including how to take part, is available on our.
[patient-facing platform][114] This resource explains what participation involves and helps you find
trials that may be relevant to you.

### Corporate information and visits

#### Can I visit Roche offices, including the headquarters in Basel?

Yes. Information on visiting Roche in Basel, including available tours and how to book, is available
at [visit-roche.ch.][115] Please note that visits typically require advance booking due to security
and operational considerations.

#### I cannot find the information I am looking for. What should I do?

If your question is not covered here, please contact us through the general requests form available
on our website. Providing a brief description of your request helps us direct it to the most
appropriate team.

# Viral Hepatitis

[An older woman with short gray hair and glasses gazes thoughtfully out a window, wearing a
patterned black blouse, in a softly lit room.]

Viral hepatitis is a major public health threat and a leading cause of death worldwide.¹ An
estimated 354 million people are living with hepatitis B or C, leading to around 1.1 million deaths
per year. That means one person dies every 30 seconds as a result of hepatitis infection.²

At Roche, we believe that everyone deserves to get tested for hepatitis. We recognise that
accessible, reliable diagnostics are key to delivering on the WHO’s target of eliminating the virus
by 2030.

#### What is viral hepatitis?

Hepatitis is a term used to describe inflammation of the liver. It causes a range of health problems
and can be fatal.1 Although some forms of hepatitis can be caused by factors like autoimmune
diseases, obesity and alcohol, most cases are caused by one of five different hepatitis viruses:
types A, B, C, D and E.

All hepatitis viruses can cause acute infection and inflammation of the liver, but infection with
hepatitis B, C, D and E can also result in chronic hepatitis. This can lead to cirrhosis and
subsequently liver cancer.6

##### In a world where hepatitis testing and treatment have been made more accessible, what’s
##### stopping people from getting tested?

People with a history of drug and needle use, high risk sexual behaviors and prisoners are often at
higher risk for hepatitis. It can also be spread from infected pregnant women to their babies.
However, many are reluctant to get screened for fear of being labeled as someone “who deserves it”.
In many low and middle income countries (LMIC’s) testing and treatment remain beyond reach for most
people.

The campaign* Everyone deserves to get tested, *aims to destigmatise these groups among the general
public, and encourage people not to let silence come in the way of getting screened. No matter who
you are, or how you got it, everyone deserves to get tested for hepatitis.

## Challenge

Testing and treatment for hepatitis remain beyond reach for most patients. With 80% of hepatitis C
infections and 90% of hepatitis B infections going undiagnosed globally,3,4 the vast majority of
patients never receive a diagnosis.

Societal attitudes and taboos not only discourage individuals from seeking testing, but also
perpetuates a harmful culture of silence surrounding the disease. We believe that silence shouldn’t
prevent people from getting screened for hepatitis.

## Focus

Diagnostics are critical both to our ability to manage viral hepatitis, and to efforts to eliminate
it. An accurate diagnosis can allow patients to access appropriate and potentially curative
treatments, reducing the likelihood that they will go on to develop chronic disease, and minimising
the risk of serious complications like cancer.5 It also enables patients to take appropriate steps
to prevent onward transmission of the virus, reducing overall infections.

# Resources and Raw Materials

[she_resources_and_raw_materials]

#### Raw materials

In buying and using raw materials, we strive to conserve resources, avoid damage to the environment
and protect the health of our employees and the public. In line with the company’s commitment to
Sustainable Development and based on the Precautionary Principle it is Roche's responsibility and
intention to avoid any actual or potential unacceptable risk arising from the use of environmental
damaging compounds.

We also invite our suppliers to work jointly with us on improving supply chain sustainability. By
engaging proactively, we aim to promote innovation, manage performance and risk, ensure business
continuity and form emergency response plans. Roche’s suppliers are asked to commit to the
principles outlined in the Roche Supplier Code of Conduct.

[read more about the Roche SCOC suppliers][103]

#### Energy

For Roche, energy consumption is a material issue. As part of our commitment to a sustainable
development and the responsible use of resources, we continuously endeavour to cut energy
consumption while increasing the proportion of sustainable energy. Our strategy is to reduce our use
first, then look for ways to substitute fossil fuels with sustainable energy.

##### A systematic approach

We seek to improve energy efficiency throughout our global operations. This, in turn, will reduce
the environmental impact, the strain on the energy supply chain and costs. Our systematic approach
to energy management includes:
* constructing energy-efficient buildings
* retrofitting heating, cooling and air conditioning installations
* adjusting the range of acceptable temperatures in offices and other workplaces
* purchasing energy-efficient equipment, including hybrid and diesel-efficient cars
* changing work processes
* reviewing employees’ travel needs

[Our position on energy conservation][104]

#### Water

Roche is dependent on clean water for the production of pharmaceutical and diagnostic goods. We
support global efforts to protect and conserve water and to improve access to clean drinking water.
Our efforts to stabilise water consumption have resulted in our water use remaining relatively
unchanged over the past five years, despite the growth of the company.

We adopt water conservation and reduction programmes according to local conditions and needs. For
example, our Californian sites use drought resistant landscaping. We reduce water consumption at
other sites by:
* collecting and recycling water from cooling towers, creating a closed-loop system
* reusing cleaning water for next ‘first rinse’ and recycling used water
* reducing cooling requirements and improving cooling processes
* improving heat recovery resulting in lower cooling water demand

[Our position on water emissions][105]

# Lunsumio (mosunetuzumab) ▼

Lunsumio is a CD20xCD3 T-cell engaging bispecific antibody. Lunsumio is approved in the EU for the
treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma who have received at
least two prior systemic therapies.

Lunsumio is a first-in-class fixed-duration CD20xCD3 T-cell engaging bispecific antibody. Lunsumio
is approved in more than 50 countries, including the EU and the US, for the treatment of adult
patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma who have received at least two prior
systemic therapies.

# Code of conduct

Defining how we do business - every day, everywhere

[Close-up of a hand holding a pen over an open notebook, suggesting active note-taking. The
background is blurred, evoking focus and concentration.]

The Roche Group Code of Conduct states the expectations Roche has as an employer towards employees
and sets forth the standards for business behaviour that apply throughout the Roche Group.

### Fostering a compliance culture

All employees and all others acting on behalf of Roche must comply with the Roche Group Code of
Conduct, regardless of their location and the nature of their work. Also, following the “One Roche
Approach” principle, the set forth standards are equally binding for Group Functions, the
Pharmaceutical and the Diagnostics Division.

The Roche Group Code of Conduct is built on the Roche Values. The code contains guidance in the
areas of products and services, personal integrity, corporate integrity, employment, company assets,
responsible business and comprehensive compliance management. It also provides questions and
answers, examples and information on where to find more detailed guidance on the various topics.
Roche employees, as well as business critical business partners, are trained on the key compliance
principles by a global mandatory eLearning. The eLearning focuses on the following topics: bribery &
improper advantages, gifts & entertainment, conflict of interest, discrimination & harassment,
responsible use of social media & electronic communication tools, and business partners & supply
chain. All employees are required to complete this eLearning when they join Roche, as well as when
the Roche Group Code of Conduct gets updated every 5 years.

Roche is corporate member of numerous pharma and diagnostics/medical device associations and adheres
to the selfregulating Code of Conducts, including IFPMA, EFPIA, MedTech Europe, APACMed, MecoMed.
Also on local level, Roche Affiliates are often member of the local associations, as for example
interpharma, scienceindustries, Advamed US, Advamed China.

### Reporting Incidents

Anyone who becomes aware of a potential violation of the Roche Group Code of Conduct can and should
bring it to the attention of our Compliance experts.

The external [Roche Group speak-up channel][103] is available for everyone who is not a Roche
employee or contractor.

Roche employees and contractors can use the following reporting channels:
* The [Roche Group Code of Conduct Help & Advice Line][104] in case of compliance questions or
uncertainties and
* The [Roche Group speak-up channel,][105] to report in good faith a suspected violation, including
a person they believe has done, is doing or may be about to do something that violates the Roche
Group Code of Conduct or constitutes a workplace incident. The Roche Group speak-up channel is a
web-based service that allows for the confidential and anonymous reporting of compliance concerns,
using either written or voice formats. The speak-up channel operates in 104 countries and 42
languages, making it available worldwide

### Non-Retaliation Policy

Any employee who raises a compliance concern in good faith acts in the interest of Roche and
deserves acknowledgment. Roche does not tolerate any retaliation against an employee who raises a
compliance concern in good faith. Line Managers and/or employees who retaliate will be held
accountable. In case any employee deems that this principle is not adhered to, a complaint can and
should be raised to the Chief Compliance Officer.

Equally, Roche does not tolerate any abuse of the Roche speak-up channels.

### Process for adequate handling of non-compliant cases

Roche takes all non-compliance reports seriously and is fully committed to efficiently and timely
investigate them, to assess the facts and, if necessary, to take adequate corrective measures and
sanctions.

Our **Business Ethics Incident Management System (BEIMS)** enables our Management, the Chief
Compliance Officer and the Chief Group Audit and Risk Advisory Executive to capture, track and
monitor alleged violations, from initial reports through to resolution.

In 2025, 614 reports were received on the speak up channels. Of these, 242 were unfounded, 301 were
found. As a result 70 employment contracts and 2 agreements with business partners were terminated
on grounds of unethical behaviour, 123 led to a warning, 2 to bonus reduction. The rest of the
founded reports resulted in corrective measures.

## A Trusted Partner of Life Science Research and the Biopharmaceutical Industry


We are living in the bio-century. Global medical knowledge is expanding at a rapid pace. But despite
huge breakthroughs, many diseases, such as cancer, rheumatism or Alzheimer's, are still not
curable.  Sartorius is part of the solution.

We help to ensure that new scientific discoveries can be translated more quickly into effective
patient care. With technologies, platforms and partnerships for a common goal: better health for
more people.

all_classified.company_summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific is a leading provider of scientific instruments, reagents, and consumables, serving a diverse range of markets including biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, clinical diagnostics, and industrial applications. The company offers a comprehensive portfolio of products and services, including antibodies, cell culture solutions, mass spectrometers, and lab instrument services, aimed at accelerating scientific discovery and improving laboratory efficiency. With a commitment to innovation and customer support, Thermo Fisher empowers researchers and organizations to make significant advancements in their fields.

all_classified.polished_summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific is a leading provider of scientific instruments, reagents, and consumables, serving a diverse range of markets including biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, clinical diagnostics, and industrial applications. The company offers a comprehensive portfolio of products and services, including antibodies, cell culture solutions, mass spectrometers, and lab instrument services, aimed at accelerating scientific discovery and improving laboratory efficiency. With a commitment to innovation and customer support, Thermo Fisher empowers researchers and organizations to make significant advancements in their fields.

all_classified.company_summary: WuXi AppTec is a leading global Contract Research, Development, and Manufacturing Organization (CRDMO) that offers a comprehensive range of R&D and manufacturing services to the pharmaceutical and life sciences industries. Its core products include WuXi Chemistry, WuXi Biology, and WuXi Testing, which support drug development from discovery to commercialization, provide extensive biology services, and deliver integrated testing solutions. Targeting pharmaceutical and biotech companies, WuXi AppTec is dedicated to enabling innovative medicines and treatments for various diseases.

## About us

As a global CRDMO (Contract Research, Development and Manufacturing Organization) with operations
across Asia, Europe, and North America, we provide global pharmaceutical services with innovators to
turn scientific discoveries into real-world therapies. Through its unique business models, WuXi
AppTec’s integrated, end-to-end solutions include chemistry drug CRDMO, biology discovery,
preclinical testing and clinical research services, helping customers improve the productivity of
advancing healthcare products in a cost-effective and efficient way. Our fully integrated platform
supports every stage of the drug development journey—from early drug discovery and preclinical
testing to clinical development and commercial manufacturing. Since we started in 2000, doing the
right thing for patients is behind everything we do. Trusted by customers across over 30 countries,
we help accelerate timelines to bring breakthrough treatments to the patients who need them most.
What drives each one of us is simple: a shared vision that every drug can be made, and every disease
can be treated.

# Overview

WuXi AppTec's broad and integrated portfolio of services enables our customers and partners in the

[Overview]
WuXi AppTec's broad and integrated portfolio of services enables our customers and partners in the
pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device industries worldwide to research, develop, discover and
produce innovative healthcare products quickly and effectively.
[Biology]
Biology
WuXi Biology provides a full spectrum of services and solutions to support stand-alone and
integrated projects, from target discovery to candidate selection and into the clinic. Our
world-class discovery platform is backed by nearly 3000 scientists, offering expertise in all major
disease areas and target classes, across all therapeutic modalities. From small molecules, peptides,
oligonucleotides to biologics, our state-of-the-art services, quick study launches and fast
turnaround times meet the diverse needs of our clients.
[LEARN MORE ][16]
[Small Molecule (CRDMO)]
Small Molecule (CRDMO)
We deliver small molecule solutions that are as powerful as they are personalized. From discovery to
market, our integrated CRDMO model simplifies your journey, providing the speed, quality and agility
your products and patients deserve—because we care, and we deliver.
[LEARN MORE ][17]
[Drug R&D Testing]
Drug R&D Testing
WuXi AppTec’s Laboratory Testing Division provides comprehensive, globally integrated CRDMO-enabling
solutions for pharmaceutical companies advancing small molecules, biologics, and emerging
therapeutic modalities. The division delivers end-to-end DMPK services, safety assessments, and
bioanalytical support throughout the development pipeline. With extensive experience in novel
compound classes including PROTACs, oligonucleotides, and ADCs, the team combines scientific
expertise, deep regulatory insight, and operational agility to accelerate drug development
timelines.

TIDES CRDMO

discover, develop and commercialize new medicines and healthcare products for patients. Under Dr.
Li’s direction, WuXi AppTec has grown into a leading global company, providing comprehensive
research, development and manufacturing services in small molecule drugs, and emerging new
modalities. Through its unique CRDMO business models, WuXi AppTec is enabling innovative partners
globally. Dr. Li earned his doctoral degree in organic chemistry from Columbia University.

driving the industry forward. Formerly Director of Technical Operations at Vertex. Bachelor's degree
in Chemistry from Peking University and Ph.D. in Organic Chemistry from the University of Minnesota.

Its core products include WuXi Chemistry, WuXi Biology, and WuXi Testing, which support drug development from discovery to commercialization, provide extensive biology services, and deliver integrated testing solutions. Targeting pharmaceutical and biotech companies, WuXi AppTec is dedicated to enabling innovative medicines and treatments for various diseases.

# Aldevron and Integrated DNA Technologies Manufacture
# World’s First mRNA-based Personalized CRISPR Therapy

Aldevron and Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT) announce the successful manufacture of the **world’s
first personalized CRISPR gene editing drug product** to treat an infant with urea cycle disorder
(UCD).

*• N of 1 therapy uniquely developed, on demand, for infant with life-threatening rare metabolic
disorder in six months*

*• Results published in The New England Journal of Medicine and showcased at American Society of
Gene & Cell Therapy Annual Meeting*

[Discover the Breakthrough][12]

## Driving Therapeutic Progress from Discovery to Commercialization

Aldevron offers comprehensive manufacturing solutions and regulatory support, ensuring unparalleled
quality and scalability for both viral and non-viral vector therapies. Our established custom
manufacturing workflows and catalog products simplify the client journey from discovery through
clinical trials to commercialization. Aldevron’s proficiency and dedication empower our partners in
genomic medicine to advance their therapeutic projects with confidence, achieving groundbreaking
success.

[Picture]

**Gene Therapy**

Unmatched expertise in plasmid design (both traditional and next-generation Nanoplasmid), process
development, and QC designed to meet viral and non-viral gene therapy applications.

[Learn More][13]

[Picture]

**Gene-Modified Cell Therapy**

Manufacturing of custom Lentiviral plasmids or use of the standardized ALD-Lenti System packaging
plasmids designed to balance availability, quality, performance, and reproducibility.

[Learn More][14]

[Picture]

**Gene Editing**

A full suite of high-quality products and services to support *ex vivo* and *in vivo* gene editing
programs from discovery to clinical, including custom and catalog nucleases and gRNA (via IDT).

[Learn More][15]

[Picture]

**RNA Vaccines & Therapeutics**

A complete service brings together RNA design, drug substance manufacturing, LNP encapsulation,
fill/finish, and analytics all under one roof and quality system.

[Learn More][16]

Standardization offers efficiency, cost savings, and may help alleviate supply chain concerns. In

### Certifications & Inspections

In June 2024, Aldevron received a Certificate of GMP Compliance of a Manufacturer from the competent
authority of Germany for an inspection. The scope of the certificate is for mRNA as an active
ingredient in the production of vaccines for clinical trials – Not Sterile.

The Breakthrough manufacturing facility was visited by the Center for Biologics Evaluation &
Research (CBER) in November 2021. CBER conducted a Pre-License Inspection (PLI) and a general GMP
audit of Aldevron, LLC. No Form FDA 483 was issued, and the inspection was classified as no action
indicated (NAI)

In July 2024, Aldevron’s Innovate Facility in Madison, WI received a renewal of its [ISO 13485:2016
certification][30] for development and manufacture of proteins for in vitro diagnostics and advanced
proteins.

all_classified.company_summary: Alira Health is a global healthcare consultancy that collaborates with life sciences companies to provide patient-centered solutions throughout the product lifecycle. The company offers a range of integrated services, including clinical research organization (CRO) services, consulting, patient engagement training, and innovative technology platforms like SpherePX™ and Health Storylines™, all aimed at enhancing patient engagement and healthcare innovation. With a focus on pharmaceuticals, medical technology, and biotechnology, Alira Health is dedicated to humanizing healthcare in partnership with patients.

# Who We Are

Alira Health is a global healthcare consultancy that partners with life sciences companies to
deliver patient-centered solutions. We generate and apply evidence across the product lifecycle
through four integrated capabilities: CRO services, consulting, patient engagement training, and
technology. Our approach helps clients improve access, adoption, and impact, guided by the voice of
the patient.

#### Our Mission Shapes Our Today and Our Vision Prepares Us for Tomorrow

We humanize healthcare and life sciences, **in partnership with patients**, through innovative
technologies and expert guidance to have a positive impact on the life of every patient.

We are a global company with the mission to humanize healthcare and life sciences, in partnership
with patients, through innovative technologies and expert guidance. We are accountable at every turn
of the biopharma and medical technology development cycle. We bring to market a new model of
solutions and services to advance the democratization of life sciences research.”

~ **Gabriele Brambilla**
Chief Executive Officer

[Gabriele Brambilla]

sciences ecosystem

##### Development

##### Consulting
##### Solutions

We put the patient’s perspective at heart of our Consulting Services. As a strategic partner, we

##### Solutions

“Evidence generation with purpose” is our motto. We address the needs of multiple stakeholders and

Our next generation patient-centric technology platform, **Health Storylines™ **captures the voice
of the patient for healthcare innovation.

### Our Values

We pride ourselves on delivering a vibrant, creative, and entrepreneurial environment where walls
and glass ceilings do not hold back initiative. Every day, this work is driven by our shared values:

#### Be Accountable
* Be accountable to all stakeholders
* Stand by our words and commitments
* Deliver what we promise, every time, in compliance with regulations and laws

#### Be Courageous
* Take chances, speak up, and try new things
* Grow beyond comfort zones to try new opportunities
* Stay on top by taking bold moves and calculated risks

#### Be Honest
* Be honest in every interaction, by being candid in a respectful way and with good intentions
* Empower everyone to voice their own opinion
* Foster a foundation of trust, as that is essential for honesty

#### Be Inclusive
* Embrace differences and show respect for everyone through words and actions
* Actively seek out differing opinions, mindsets and cultures, as that enriches all of us,
personally and professionally
* Share knowledge and experience with others, freeing us all to operate on a higher level

#### Elevate Others
* Support and actively nurture other people to be their best, as everyone has something valuable to
share
* Look for opportunities to praise, acknowledge, support and contribute to the advantage of others
* Provide professional development opportunities, and elevate our teams’ abilities to better serve
our clients

Using these ideals as our daily touchstones, we work closely with each client, and each other, to
identify and complement their expertise with a full spectrum of support.

### Investing in Our Communities

As part of our commitment to our mission and shared values, we work with our local and global
communities to create positive change through education, service, and sustainable business
practices.

# Who We Are

Alira Health is a global healthcare consultancy that partners with life sciences companies to
deliver patient-centered solutions. We generate and apply evidence across the product lifecycle
through four integrated capabilities: CRO services, consulting, patient engagement training, and
technology. Our approach helps clients improve access, adoption, and impact, guided by the voice of
the patient.

#### Our Mission Shapes Our Today and Our Vision Prepares Us for Tomorrow

We humanize healthcare and life sciences, **in partnership with patients**, through innovative
technologies and expert guidance to have a positive impact on the life of every patient.

We are a global company with the mission to humanize healthcare and life sciences, in partnership
with patients, through innovative technologies and expert guidance. We are accountable at every turn
of the biopharma and medical technology development cycle. We bring to market a new model of
solutions and services to advance the democratization of life sciences research.”

~ **Gabriele Brambilla**
Chief Executive Officer

[Gabriele Brambilla]

[ Learn more ][84]

### Our Value Is in Our Patient Focus

A patient-first attitude and desire to make our business a force for good in the healthcare and life
sciences ecosystem

##### Research & Clinical
##### Development

Our team offers experienced, multidisciplinary guidance, and support for all aspects of your
clinical trial. As a full-service CRO, our offering is designed to successfully execute studies, in
all phases in a wide range of therapeutic areas, that deliver results ready for regulatory use.

##### Consulting
##### Solutions

We put the patient’s perspective at heart of our Consulting Services. As a strategic partner, we
deliver more than recommendations – we create achievable strategies rooted in research, backed by
advanced analytics, and supported through execution.

##### Real-World
##### Solutions

“Evidence generation with purpose” is our motto. We address the needs of multiple stakeholders and
customers, with the participation of patients as drivers, for their ultimate benefit.

##### Patient-Centric Technology Platform

Our next generation patient-centric technology platform, **Health Storylines™ **captures the voice
of the patient for healthcare innovation.

### Our Values

We pride ourselves on delivering a vibrant, creative, and entrepreneurial environment where walls
and glass ceilings do not hold back initiative. Every day, this work is driven by our shared values:

#### Be Accountable
* Be accountable to all stakeholders
* Stand by our words and commitments
* Deliver what we promise, every time, in compliance with regulations and laws

#### Be Courageous
* Take chances, speak up, and try new things
* Grow beyond comfort zones to try new opportunities
* Stay on top by taking bold moves and calculated risks

#### Be Honest
* Be honest in every interaction, by being candid in a respectful way and with good intentions
* Empower everyone to voice their own opinion
* Foster a foundation of trust, as that is essential for honesty

#### Be Inclusive
* Embrace differences and show respect for everyone through words and actions
* Actively seek out differing opinions, mindsets and cultures, as that enriches all of us,
personally and professionally
* Share knowledge and experience with others, freeing us all to operate on a higher level

#### Elevate Others
* Support and actively nurture other people to be their best, as everyone has something valuable to
share
* Look for opportunities to praise, acknowledge, support and contribute to the advantage of others
* Provide professional development opportunities, and elevate our teams’ abilities to better serve
our clients

Using these ideals as our daily touchstones, we work closely with each client, and each other, to
identify and complement their expertise with a full spectrum of support.

### Investing in Our Communities

As part of our commitment to our mission and shared values, we work with our local and global
communities to create positive change through education, service, and sustainable business
practices.

The company offers a wide range of publications, multimedia content, and educational resources aimed at professionals in the biopharma sector, including insights on biologics, biosimilars, and innovative drug delivery systems. With a focus on enhancing industry knowledge and facilitating partnerships, Bio Pharminternational serves as a vital hub for stakeholders in the biopharmaceutical landscape.

The company offers a diverse range of products, including recombinant proteins, assay kits, and chromatography reagents, aimed at enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of scientific research and drug development. Our Story

## First in finance-specific LLM software

Founded in 2019 as an AI research team during the early LLM era, Hudson Labs was the first
finance-specific software to be completely powered by language models.

Hudson Labs' unique contributions to financial AI research include proprietary relevance ranking
techniques, noise suppression, boilerplate removal and mathematical reasoning.

Today, we serve institutional investors managing over $1 trillion in assets, providing them with
research tools that combine the precision of a financial terminal with the adaptability of
artificial intelligence.

About

# State-of-the-Art Financial AI R&D

Founded in 2019 as an AI research team during the early LLM era. Hudson Labs was the first
finance-specific software to be completely powered by language models.

Our Story

## First in finance-specific LLM software

Founded in 2019 as an AI research team during the early LLM era, Hudson Labs was the first
finance-specific software to be completely powered by language models.

Hudson Labs' unique contributions to financial AI research include proprietary relevance ranking
techniques, noise suppression, boilerplate removal and mathematical reasoning.

Today, we serve institutional investors managing over $1 trillion in assets, providing them with
research tools that combine the precision of a financial terminal with the adaptability of
artificial intelligence.

## Anyone can say they're an expert.

But only one of us wrote the textbook.

*Designing Large Language Model Applications*by Suhas Pai, Co-founder & CTO, Hudson Labs. Published
by O'Reilly Media.

[Designing Large Language Model Applications - O'Reilly book by Suhas Pai]

Leadership

## Founded by domain experts

[Kris Bennatti, CEO & Co-Founder at Hudson Labs]

### Kris Bennatti

CEO & Co-Founder

Prior to founding Hudson Labs, Kris worked as the lead data scientist at corporate governance
advisory firm, Hansell McLaughlin and taught Python programming at an AI boot camp. Kris is CPA, CA
(inactive) and has a masters degree in data analytics from the Schulich School of Business and an
undergraduate degree in Accounting and Economics from McGill University.

[Suhas Pai, CTO & Co-Founder at Hudson Labs]

### Suhas Pai

CTO & Co-Founder

Suhas is a well-known applied AI, natural language processing and machine learning researcher. He is
the author of the popular textbook, Designing Large Language Model Applications published by
O'Reilly Media. He was the Privacy co-chair at Big Science for the BLOOM LLM, which at the time of
its release was the world's largest open-source multilingual LLM, along with contributions to
various other LLMs and their training datasets. He has been the chair of the Toronto Machine
Learning Summit for the last four years. Suhas has a Masters degree in Computer Science from
Eindhoven University of Technology in The Netherlands, and spent over five years at IBM where he
held the position of Staff Software Engineer.

For those with a stake in Philadelphia — people looking to thrive where they live, and those who
want to keep their finger on the pulse of what makes Philly, Philly — The Philadelphia Inquirer is
your essential source of information in the city and region. No other news organization is as deeply
rooted in Philadelphia or better understands what makes it tick, from the communities of Chinatown
to the playgrounds of West Philly to the suburbs of our surrounding counties, than [The
Inquirer.][61]

## Journalism Ethics

Tim Tai / Staff Photographer

## Accuracy
* We strive for accuracy, and we correct errors as quickly as possible online and in print.
* We do not plagiarize or use another outlet’s work without proper attribution and credit.
* We do not significantly alter quotations, photographs, videos, or audio recordings in ways that
change their meaning or context.

## Fairness
* We are fair-minded and thorough in our reporting.
* We seek a diversity of opinions and sources.
* We aim for journalism that is free of favoritism or bias and that minimizes undue harm.

Tom Gralish / Staff Photographer
José F. Moreno / Staff Photographer

## Independence
* We avoid potential conflicts of interests or any action that may compromise the credibility of our
news reporting. We also avoid business relationships that would compromise our credibility.
* We provide a distinction between our news report and advertising content, with clear
identification of any content that is sponsored or grant-funded.
* We do not offer money or favors for interviews or information, nor do we accept gifts from
sources.

## Trust
* We recognize that the trust of our audiences is our most valuable asset.
* We identify ourselves as Inquirer journalists when reporting and always aim for clear attribution;
anonymous sourcing is carefully vetted and avoided if possible.
* We seek to gain understanding of the communities, people, and issues we cover to provide an
informed account of our region.

Jessica Griffin / Staff Photographer
Michael Bryant / Staff Photographer

## Integrity
* We act with professional and personal integrity, and we demonstrate that in our interactions with
sources and readers.
* We seek solutions in addition to exposing problems.
* We provide free access to essential news coverage during public safety emergencies and as a public
service when appropriate.

Tim Tai / Staff Photographer

## Accuracy
* We strive for accuracy, and we correct errors as quickly as possible online and in print.
* We do not plagiarize or use another outlet’s work without proper attribution and credit.
* We do not significantly alter quotations, photographs, videos, or audio recordings in ways that
change their meaning or context.

## Company Values

Our people are critical to achieving our shared mission and goals. By prioritizing how we treat and
interact with one another, we are better positioned to drive our long-term sustainability. Our
internal company values define and guide how we work together.

Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer
Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer

## Optimism
* We care deeply about The Inquirer’s mission and its importance to Philadelphia and the region, as
well as driving our business sustainability for decades to come.
* We challenge long-held assumptions and the status quo, and we remain flexible to best serve our
customers and community.
* We celebrate our wins, learn from our failures, and embrace the ongoing change and challenges
required to achieve our mission.

Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer
Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer

## Inclusion
* We are committed to being a diverse, inclusive, equitable, and anti-racist organization in how we
operate through workplace culture, coverage of news, and community relations.
* We work to mitigate our biases, develop our cultural competence, and practice allyship to ensure
all employees, regardless of background and identity, feel valued and a sense of belonging.
* We continuously adapt to the ever-changing landscape through ongoing learning, improvement, and
self-reflection.

Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer
Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer

## Collaboration
* We partner to achieve our shared goals, solve problems, and make decisions, prioritizing outcomes
that are in the best interest of The Inquirer, our mission, and our customers.
* We break down silos to engage in purposeful cross-functional teamwork.
* We value and invite each other’s diverse perspectives, experiences, and ideas to fuel innovation
and our transformation.

Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer
Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer

## Openness
* We listen attentively, seek to understand before responding, and engage in civil debate.
* We are timely and consistent in sharing relevant information with each other.
* We build trust, connection, and respect across the company.

Elizabeth Robertson / Staff Photographer
Elizabeth Robertson / Staff Photographer

## Empowerment
* We take personal responsibility for our goals and behavior, admit mistakes, and share our
learnings with others.
* We seek and give constructive feedback to ensure all of us are growing and developing.
* We rally behind our shared mission with enthusiasm, and we support our direction and the decisions
that are made.

## Our Ownership Structure

The Lenfest Institute is the non-profit, non-controlling owner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. [The
Institute][62] creates solutions for the next era of local news by investing in sustainable business
models at the intersection of local journalism and community in Philadelphia and also nationwide.
The Institute supports The Inquirer’s investments in technology and digital products to best serve
its audiences and to reach new ones, as well as in The Inquirer’s investigative journalism. Support
The Lenfest Institute’s work with The Inquirer by donating to The Inquirer’s[ High-Impact Journalism
Fund][63].

For those with a stake in Philadelphia — people looking to thrive where they live, and those who
want to keep their finger on the pulse of what makes Philly, Philly — The Philadelphia Inquirer is
your essential source of information in the city and region. No other news organization is as deeply
rooted in Philadelphia or better understands what makes it tick, from the communities of Chinatown
to the playgrounds of West Philly to the suburbs of our surrounding counties, than [The
Inquirer.][61]

## Journalism Ethics

Tim Tai / Staff Photographer

## Accuracy
* We strive for accuracy, and we correct errors as quickly as possible online and in print.
* We do not plagiarize or use another outlet’s work without proper attribution and credit.
* We do not significantly alter quotations, photographs, videos, or audio recordings in ways that
change their meaning or context.

## Fairness
* We are fair-minded and thorough in our reporting.
* We seek a diversity of opinions and sources.
* We aim for journalism that is free of favoritism or bias and that minimizes undue harm.

Tom Gralish / Staff Photographer
José F. Moreno / Staff Photographer

## Independence
* We avoid potential conflicts of interests or any action that may compromise the credibility of our
news reporting. We also avoid business relationships that would compromise our credibility.
* We provide a distinction between our news report and advertising content, with clear
identification of any content that is sponsored or grant-funded.
* We do not offer money or favors for interviews or information, nor do we accept gifts from
sources.

## Trust
* We recognize that the trust of our audiences is our most valuable asset.
* We identify ourselves as Inquirer journalists when reporting and always aim for clear attribution;
anonymous sourcing is carefully vetted and avoided if possible.
* We seek to gain understanding of the communities, people, and issues we cover to provide an
informed account of our region.

Jessica Griffin / Staff Photographer
Michael Bryant / Staff Photographer

## Integrity
* We act with professional and personal integrity, and we demonstrate that in our interactions with
sources and readers.
* We seek solutions in addition to exposing problems.
* We provide free access to essential news coverage during public safety emergencies and as a public
service when appropriate.

Tim Tai / Staff Photographer

## Company Values

Our people are critical to achieving our shared mission and goals. By prioritizing how we treat and
interact with one another, we are better positioned to drive our long-term sustainability. Our
internal company values define and guide how we work together.

Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer
Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer

## Optimism
* We care deeply about The Inquirer’s mission and its importance to Philadelphia and the region, as
well as driving our business sustainability for decades to come.
* We challenge long-held assumptions and the status quo, and we remain flexible to best serve our
customers and community.
* We celebrate our wins, learn from our failures, and embrace the ongoing change and challenges
required to achieve our mission.

Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer
Tyger Williams / Staff Photographer

## Inclusion
* We are committed to being a diverse, inclusive, equitable, and anti-racist organization in how we
operate through workplace culture, coverage of news, and community relations.
* We work to mitigate our biases, develop our cultural competence, and practice allyship to ensure
all employees, regardless of background and identity, feel valued and a sense of belonging.
* We continuously adapt to the ever-changing landscape through ongoing learning, improvement, and
self-reflection.

Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer
Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer

## Collaboration
* We partner to achieve our shared goals, solve problems, and make decisions, prioritizing outcomes
that are in the best interest of The Inquirer, our mission, and our customers.
* We break down silos to engage in purposeful cross-functional teamwork.
* We value and invite each other’s diverse perspectives, experiences, and ideas to fuel innovation
and our transformation.

Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer
Heather Khalifa / Staff Photographer

## Openness
* We listen attentively, seek to understand before responding, and engage in civil debate.
* We are timely and consistent in sharing relevant information with each other.
* We build trust, connection, and respect across the company.

Elizabeth Robertson / Staff Photographer
Elizabeth Robertson / Staff Photographer

## Empowerment
* We take personal responsibility for our goals and behavior, admit mistakes, and share our
learnings with others.
* We seek and give constructive feedback to ensure all of us are growing and developing.
* We rally behind our shared mission with enthusiasm, and we support our direction and the decisions
that are made.

all_classified.company_summary: Octapharma is one of the largest human protein manufacturers globally, specializing in the development and production of life-saving therapies derived from human cell lines and plasma. The company focuses on key therapeutic areas, including haematology, immunotherapy, and critical care, providing essential medicines that support patients with bleeding disorders, immune system deficiencies, and critical illnesses. With a commitment to innovation and sustainability, Octapharma aims to advance human life through its extensive research and development efforts.

all_classified.polished_summary: Octapharma is one of the largest human protein manufacturers globally, specializing in the development and production of life-saving therapies derived from human cell lines and plasma. The company focuses on key therapeutic areas, including haematology, immunotherapy, and critical care, providing essential medicines that support patients with bleeding disorders, immune system deficiencies, and critical illnesses. With a commitment to innovation and sustainability, Octapharma aims to advance human life through its extensive research and development efforts.

## About Us

### Note from the Editor

Welcome to *Pharma's Almanac*, a pioneering thought leadership publication shining a light on
trends, topics, and innovations in life sciences. For years, I've had the privilege of collaborating
with dynamic thought leaders throughout the biopharmaceutical field — from scientists to executives,
encompassing drug discovery, development, manufacturing, and logistics — to tell informative and
engaging stories at the forefront of the industry.

At *Pharma's Almanac*, our mission is to explore the challenges and advances in biopharma and life
sciences. We are passionate about providing comprehensive yet accessible written and video content
that covers the latest hurdles, trends, and breakthroughs in the industry. From advanced therapies
at the bleeding edge of molecular innovation to the intricate balance of global and local concerns
in the supply chain, we aim to connect our readers with leading subject matter experts.

[about us]

### Write With Us

Are you working on a project that you want to share with the greater biopharmaceutical industry? Or
maybe you have a unique perspective that you believe can shape industry discourse? We are always
looking for new voices to join our team of writers and storytellers. If you're interested, email me
at [editors@pharmasalmanac.com][18] and let’s discuss how we can collaborate.

[Get In Touch][19]

### Nice Insight: The Research & Analytical Expertise Driving Our Content

*Pharma's Almanac* works closely with Nice Insight, the research division of [That’s Nice][20], to
sharpen our stories with hard-to-find data and exclusive analysis. Explore how Nice Insight tracks
life science trends with all-in-one market research reports and custom research projects.

## About Us

### Note from the Editor

Welcome to *Pharma's Almanac*, a pioneering thought leadership publication shining a light on
trends, topics, and innovations in life sciences. For years, I've had the privilege of collaborating
with dynamic thought leaders throughout the biopharmaceutical field — from scientists to executives,
encompassing drug discovery, development, manufacturing, and logistics — to tell informative and
engaging stories at the forefront of the industry.

At *Pharma's Almanac*, our mission is to explore the challenges and advances in biopharma and life
sciences. We are passionate about providing comprehensive yet accessible written and video content
that covers the latest hurdles, trends, and breakthroughs in the industry. From advanced therapies
at the bleeding edge of molecular innovation to the intricate balance of global and local concerns
in the supply chain, we aim to connect our readers with leading subject matter experts.

[about us]

### Write With Us

Are you working on a project that you want to share with the greater biopharmaceutical industry? Or
maybe you have a unique perspective that you believe can shape industry discourse? We are always
looking for new voices to join our team of writers and storytellers. If you're interested, email me
at [editors@pharmasalmanac.com][18] and let’s discuss how we can collaborate.

[Get In Touch][19]

### Nice Insight: The Research & Analytical Expertise Driving Our Content

*Pharma's Almanac* works closely with Nice Insight, the research division of [That’s Nice][20], to
sharpen our stories with hard-to-find data and exclusive analysis. Explore how Nice Insight tracks
life science trends with all-in-one market research reports and custom research projects.

[Learn More][21]

## About Us

Welcome to Phlex Proteins, where innovation meets quality in protein solutions. Since our
establishment, we've been dedicated to transforming the protein industry through cutting-edge
technology, exceptional service, and unwavering commitment to quality.

Founded by Dr. Jason Chou, Steve Brauer, and Joe Heitz, Phlex Proteins is a plant forward company
that specializes in the manufacturing and distribution of plant-based proteins and ingredients.

### The Leading Protein Provider in the Industry

We are committed to achieving this by prioritizing our customers' needs and integrating the latest
technology to ensure optimal service delivery. Through respectful partnerships, we aim to exceed our
customers' expectations and solidify our position as a top-tier protein companys.

### Mission

We strive to provide premium protein solutions that empower businesses to create exceptional
products. Our success is built on three core commitments that guide everything we do.

[Exceptional Customer Service]

###### Exceptional Customer Service

Our dedicated team understands your unique needs and provides tailored solutions. From technical
consultation to after-sales support, we ensure your success.

[High-Quality Ingredient]

###### High-Quality Ingredient

We source only the finest raw materials and maintain rigorous quality control standards. Your
reputation depends on our quality, and we take that seriously.

[Reliable Logistics Providers]

###### Reliable Logistics Providers

We partner with trusted logistics providers worldwide to ensure timely delivery. Our global
distribution network guarantees your ingredients arrive when needed.

### Leveraging our Vast Ingredient Industry Experience

With our wealth of experience in the ingredient industry, we have established a strong global
presence that extends to various markets and regions. Our adeptness in maneuvering through intricate
regulatory landscapes, cultural subtleties, and supply chain intricacies has equipped us with an
in-depth understanding of the distinct requirements and expectations of customers around the world.

As we continue to expand our global reach, we are dedicated to providing innovative solutions that
cater to the evolving needs of our valued partners and customers.

### Our Team

Every member of the Phlex family shares one commitment: delivering excellence to support your
business goals.

## We’re guided by our company values that **define our culture**

Be customer obsessed

We put customers at the center of everything we do. We strive to deeply understand their needs and
go above and beyond to exceed expectations.

Master the domain

We obsess over mastering Life Sciences communication and the Prezent Vivo ecosystem. We deeply
understand our industry, customers, their challenges, workflows, and goals, so we can deliver
unmatched value and become their trusted partners.

Win as a team

We succeed together. We lead with empathy, break down silos, and support one another—always putting
team success ahead of individual gain.

Value every dollar

We are obsessed with growth and cost efficiency. We treat every dollar as our own and spend it only
when it clearly drives customer acquisition, better customer outcomes, or business growth. We never
compromise on quality and always maximize impact.

Earn trust through relentless execution

Strategy means nothing without execution. We build deep trust by delivering with the same intensity,
quality, and urgency as our strategy, consistently turning promises into exceptional results.

> *Your deepest desire is your destiny.

Rajat is the founder and CEO of Prezent – the #1 communication success and presentation productivity
platform for enterprise teams. Powered by ASTRID - the multi-disciplinary AI communication
assistant. With Prezent teams supercharge communication effectiveness by 80%, save 70% on
presentations and reduce agency costs by 60%. Prezent serves tens of thousands of professionals in
80+ F2000 companies.He is also the President of PREZENTIUM, a tech-enabled presentation services
firm for F2000 companies.

Prior to Prezent, Rajat was a Senior Vice President at Cisco Systems where he had P&L responsibility
for Cisco's $14B CX business, led a 1000+ person team and was responsible for the Strategy, Product
Management and Marketing functions. He has served in leadership roles at Mu Sigma, McKinsey &
Company, and Microsoft Corporation.

He is the executive producer of “Think Deeply. Speak Simply” podcast. An active philanthropist, he
is on the leadership council of No Kid Hungry and advisory board of Adruta Children’s Home. He has
spoken at CES, VentureBeat and Start Up Grind. He has also been quoted in Forbes, Inc., Nasdaq, CRN,
etc.

He holds an MBA degree in strategic management from Wharton, achieving Director's List honors, and a
BSc degree in computer science and engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), where
he achieved Dean’s List honors.

Rajat has been named to Wharton Business School's "40 under 40", Silicon Valley Business Journal's
"40 under 40" and Cisco's Amazing People. He holds three patents in AI and software automation.

## FAQs

What makes Prezent different from other AI-powered presentation tools?

Other AI tools create generic slides. Prezent is built for the enterprise, incorporating your
company’s brand guidelines, communication style, and business context—so outputs are not just fast,
but also on-brand, audience-aware, and relevant.

How does Prezent ensure our brand and templates are used correctly?

We work directly with your brand or marketing teams to ensure your brand guidelines—logos, fonts,
colors, templates, etc—are correct and aligned when we onboard your team. No more “Frankenstein
decks.” Every output stays consistent, compliant, and on-brand, whether it’s made by an intern or
your CMO and it’s all approved by you.

Can I use Prezent with PowerPoint and Google Slides?

Absolutely. Prezent integrates seamlessly with both platforms. You can export decks in either format
while maintaining structure, design, and brand fidelity.

What kind of support is available?

All customers get access to in-platform help. All plan types—except our self-service option—also
include onboarding sessions and a dedicated customer success manager. You can consider our team as
an extension of your team and we pride ourselves on building high-touch, collaborative relationships
with every customer. Higher-tier plans and add-ons will unlock access to our Expert Services team
for custom design support and communication training.

Why does Prezent use custom pricing for some plans?

Every organization has unique needs—team size, brand complexity, security requirements, and the
level of support or services needed can vary widely. Custom pricing allows us to tailor a plan that
fits your exact goals and ensures you get the most value from Prezent. Whether you’re rolling it out
to a 20-person team or a global enterprise, we’ll work with you to build the right solution.

## We’re guided by our company values that **define our culture**

Be customer obsessed

We put customers at the center of everything we do. We strive to deeply understand their needs and
go above and beyond to exceed expectations.

Master the domain

We obsess over mastering Life Sciences communication and the Prezent Vivo ecosystem. We deeply
understand our industry, customers, their challenges, workflows, and goals, so we can deliver
unmatched value and become their trusted partners.

Win as a team

We succeed together. We lead with empathy, break down silos, and support one another—always putting
team success ahead of individual gain.

Value every dollar

We are obsessed with growth and cost efficiency. We treat every dollar as our own and spend it only
when it clearly drives customer acquisition, better customer outcomes, or business growth. We never
compromise on quality and always maximize impact.

Earn trust through relentless execution

Strategy means nothing without execution. We build deep trust by delivering with the same intensity,
quality, and urgency as our strategy, consistently turning promises into exceptional results.

all_classified.polished_summary: ProSpec Bio is a leading manufacturer specializing in high-quality recombinant proteins and antibodies for research and development in the life sciences sector. The company offers a diverse range of products, including cytokines, growth factors, chemokines, and both monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies, alongside molecular biology and bioprocessing services such as DNA cloning and protein expression. Targeting researchers in life sciences and biotechnology, ProSpec Bio is committed to advancing scientific discovery through its innovative solutions and expertise.

all_classified.company_summary: Protein Eng is a customer-centric biotechnology company specializing in comprehensive protein engineering services to support life sciences and drug research and development. The company offers a range of innovative services, including directed evolution, protein mutation library construction, high-throughput screening, protein synthesis, and post-translational modifications, catering primarily to biotechnology and pharmaceutical researchers across various industries such as pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and environmental services.
